cards.text: Isaiah the prophet opens with a woe for Ephraim, the northern kingdom of Israel. Nobody ever opened a letter that starts with WOE and found a coupon inside. It's aimed at a majestic crown, set on the summit above the fertile valley, right up top where the whole valley can see it.

cards.question: Isaiah's woe is for the majestic crown of Ephraim's ___.
It's a woe, not a compliment. What kind of flower does Isaiah call the glorious splendor of Ephraim's crown?

cards.text: Then Isaiah says, "Behold, the Lord has one who is strong and mighty." Isaiah never says who. He just tells you how this one shows up.

cards.question: What does Isaiah say the Lord's strong and mighty one will be like?

answers.text: A fire spreading through the forest

cards.question: The Lord's strong and mighty one will lift Ephraim's crown even higher on the summit.

cards.text: That crown will be trampled underfoot. Top of the hill to the bottom of somebody's sandal, and then Isaiah gives that fading flower on the summit one more picture.

cards.question: What will the fading flower on the summit be like?

answers.text: A ripe fig before the summer harvest
Grass that withers in the noon sun
A reed shaken by the river wind

cards.question: Whoever sees that ripe fig will leave it hanging on the tree for later.

cards.text: One look, one grab, GONE, which is exactly me in front of a cooling rack, friend. Then the picture flips: on that day the LORD of Hosts Himself will be "a crown of glory, a diadem of splendor."

cards.question: On that day, who will the LORD of Hosts be a crown of glory to?
The LORD will be a spirit of ___ to him who sits in judgment.
The LORD will also be a strength to those who repel the onslaught at the gate.

cards.text: Then Isaiah says these also stagger from wine and stumble from strong drink. And WHOO, friend, the next names on that list are not who you'd expect.

cards.question: Who does Isaiah say reels from strong drink and is befuddled by wine?
The strong drink leaves the priests and prophets muddled in their visions and stumbling in their judgments.

cards.text: Priests and prophets, friend. And Isaiah says it plainly: "For all their tables are covered with vomit; there is not a place without filth."
Then the questions come: "Whom is He trying to teach? To whom is He explaining His message?" I think somebody feels talked down to.

cards.question: The questions keep going. Who is He supposedly teaching, as if it were their very first lesson?

answers.text: Elders sitting at the city gate

cards.text: For they hear: "Order on order, order on order, line on line, line on line; a little here, a little there." That's the coworker who explains the copier one button at a time. EVERY. SINGLE. MORNING.

cards.question: Isaiah says He will speak to this people another way. How?

answers.text: With mocking lips and foreign tongues
By a voice from the clouds

cards.text: And these are people He already spoke to. He told them, "This is the place of rest, let the weary rest; this is the place of repose."

cards.question: The people listened and took the rest He offered them.

cards.text: So the word of the LORD to them will become that line again: order on order, line on line, a little here, a little there.

cards.question: When the word of the LORD becomes that line again, which way does it send the people?
Stumbling backward, they will be injured, ensnared and ___.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 10 quotes "a crown of glory, a diadem of splendor.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card says Ephraim is the northern kingdom of Israel. That fact comes from outside the passage, but the card gives no reference for it. The card cites only Isaiah 28:1, which doesn't say this.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "laughter" reads as silly next to "justice" for someone who sits in judgment. It doesn't match the tone of the other answers.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The word "supposedly" states as fact that these questions are mocking or sarcastic. Isaiah 28:9 leaves open who asks them and why. Card 5 marked this as a guess ("I think"), but card 6 drops the marker.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "So the word of the LORD to them will become..." makes verse 13 a result of the people not listening. The BSB says only "Then," so the card adds a cause-and-effect link the text doesn't state.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Stop 2 has very little of Papa Dorin's humor. The copier joke on card 7 is the only real laugh. Card 1's "WHOO, friend" is filler, and cards 4, 9 and 11 are plain retelling with no voice. Card 4's "Priests and prophets, friend." also mostly repeats card 2's answer.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
